id: P:Anton Ferdinand Troyer von Aufkirchen und Thun
summary: An Indologist, Anton Ferdinand Troyer von Aufkirchen und Thun studied at the Theresian Military Academy in 1787. He served as director of the Madras Military Institution (1807) and secretary at Sanskrit College and University (1827–1835).
Anton Gerard van Hamel was a linguist who studied at Barlaeus Gymnasium from around 1898 to 1904. He later held a post at Utrecht University from 1923 to 1945.

Anton Kogan is a linguist and Indologist who studied at the Russian State University for the Humanities from 1992 to 1997. In 2000, he became a Senior Research Fellow at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Linguist and Indologist Anton Scherer studied under Gustav Herbig, Friedrich Ernst Kieckers, and Ferdinand Sommer, earning his PhD from the University of Munich (~1927–1932). He held professorships at the University of Würzburg (1948–1951) and Heidelberg University (1951–1969).

Anton Schiefner, a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and linguistics, studied at Saint Petersburg State University and Humboldt University of Berlin under mentors including Franz Bopp. He held several posts at the Russian Academy of Sciences and directed the Peter the Great Museum.
A scholar of Buddhist studies, Anton Walter Florus Gueth served as a docent at Taisho University in 1921 and as a professor at Komazawa University in 1922.
Anton Westermann was a scholar in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Leipzig from 1825 to 1830 and served there as Mitdirektor from 1830 to 1865.

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, Anton Zigmund-Cerbu studied at the University of Bucharest, EPHE, and INALCO, supervised by Jean Filliozat and Rolf Alfred Stein. He worked at the CNRS (1952) and Columbia University (1960).

Working in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history and archaeology, Antonello Palumbo was affiliated with the Italian School of East Asian Studies as a researcher (attested 2004) and held a post at SOAS University of London (attested 2005–2010).

Linguist and Indologist Antoni Józef Śmieszek earned his Ph.D. at Jagiellonian University and studied in Berlin, Munich, and London. He was an assistant professor at Adam Mickiewicz University (1922–1935) and professor of Egyptology at the University of Warsaw (1934–1939).

Antoni Kałuski was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Jagiellonian University (1912–1915) under Jan Michał Rozwadowski and Andrzej Gawroński, and later pursued studies at the University of Chicago.

Antoni Muchliński, a linguist and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar, studied at the Imperial University of Vilna (~1823–1828) and held a post at Saint Petersburg State University from around 1835 to 1866.

Indologist Antonie Rutgers studied at the University of Groningen (~1820–1830) and at Leiden University under Hendrik Arent Hamaker. He served as extraordinary professor of Hebrew at Leiden University from 1837 to 1875.

A scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies, Antonino Forte held posts at Hōbōgirin and the EFEO (~1976–1989), the Italian School of East Asian Studies (~1989–1999), and served as professor at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~1989–2006).

Antonino Pagliaro, a scholar of linguistics, philosophy, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, studied under Christian Bartholomae and Paul Kretschmer. He was privatdozent (1926) and professor of glottology (1936–1968) at Sapienza University of Rome.

Antonio Agostino Giorgi was an Indologist and Tibetologist who studied under Giovanni Lorenzo Berti. He served as professor of sacred writings at Sapienza University of Rome from 1746 and became librarian at the Biblioteca Angelica in 1752.
Antonio Faiani was an Indologist who served as director at Liceo Classico Massimo d'Azeglio and Liceo Ariosto.
Antonio Marazzi was an Indologist who studied at the University of Turin under Giovanni Flechia.

Antonio Rigopoulos is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He completed his PhD at the University of California, Santa Barbara (1987–1994) and became a full professor at Ca' Foscari University of Venice in 1999.

Antonio T. de Nicolás worked in philosophy and Indology, earning his PhD from Fordham University (~1966–1968). He held a post at Stony Brook University from around 1969 to 1996 as professor emeritus of philosophy.
